text:
Maya Rao: Heads-up — support ticket #4521 from Acme Inc reporting a sudden p95 spike from ~120ms -> ~2.4s starting around 2026-03-15T09:32Z. They are on Dedicated pool `eu-west-2-d`.
ops-bot: alert: dedicated-pool-eu-west-2-d saturating; provisioning_queue=18, pending_attach=6, gpu_util=98%, alert_time=2026-03-15T09:30:52Z
Jordan Li: Can someone grab provisioning logs + control-plane throttle stats? Suspect scale-up backlog. Also did we fall back to hosted models for retries?
Eli Patel: pulling metrics now. p95 token latency for model v35 jumped at 09:31Z. Provisioning queue time histogram: median ~400ms, p95 ~12s, p99 ~38s. Warm-pool shows 0 available nodes in eu-west-2-d.
Samir Khan: digging into provisioner logs, paste:
```
2026-03-15T09:30:45Z provisioner ERROR attach_timeout host=gpu-3a id=pool-eu-d err=rate_limited
2026-03-15T09:30:46Z provisioner WARN queue_len=19 attempt=5 backoff=8s
2026-03-15T09:31:02Z hypertask ERROR handshake failed: ErrHandshakeTimeout
```
Maya Rao: Support says some of the customer's requests returned 500s and then visible retry storms, which bumped p99 further. They were pinned to the Dedicated pool for compliance.
Devon (support-bot): ticket update: customer-perf-impact=high, severity=P2, notified-account-team, timestamp=2026-03-15T09:34Z
Jordan Li: Two immediate hypotheses: (1) global provisioning_rate_limiter kicked in causing 429s -> retries, (2) config change to warm-pool/autoscale reduced prewarmed nodes. Who modified autoscaler in the last 24h?
Samir Khan: I changed autoscaler config yesterday to lower cost by reducing min_warm_nodes from 2 -> 0 in eu-west-2-d for a short experiment. I'm reverting now.
Eli Patel: Confirmed: control-plane logs show provisioning_rate_limiter dropped requests at 09:30:45 for project=acme (token_bucket=0). Provisioner received 429s and retried with exponential backoff which amplified attach backlog. Metrics line up with the customer's window.
Maya Rao: OK — immediate mitigation plan?
Jordan Li: 1) Temporarily raise `min_warm_nodes` back to 2 for eu-west-2-d. 2) Bump provisioner concurrency / token bucket for 15 minutes to clear queue. 3) If needed, route small % of traffic to hosted or another healthy dedicated pool as fallback.
Samir Khan: Rolling min_warm_nodes change now, and kicking off manual warm-up job to pre-create 3 nodes.
ops-bot: action: scale action queued: set pool eu-west-2-d min_warm=2 by samir@infra at 2026-03-15T09:36:12Z
Eli Patel: Post-mitigation update: after warm-up p95 dropped from ~2.4s -> ~180ms within ~6 minutes. pending_attach is 0, queue depth cleared. p99 still elevated but trending down towards baseline.
Devon (support-bot): updated ticket: mitigation applied, customer notified, monitoring for 2h. :thumbsup:
Jordan Li: Long-term follow-ups: revert the cost experiment, add guardrail to disallow min_warm_nodes < 1 for production pools, add alert when provisioning_queue > 10, and add jitter to provisioner backoff to avoid synchronized retries.
Maya Rao: Agree. Also add an automated canary that verifies min_warm_nodes per pool after config pushes.
Samir Khan: Created INFRA-1248: "Prevent zero-min warm nodes in prod + provisioning throttle observability". Owner=Samir. Includes rollback of yesterday's config, dashboard updates, and add automated warm-up job.
Eli Patel: I'll add a dashboard widget for provisioning queue depth, attach latency p95/p99, and rate_limiter drop count.
Maya Rao: Thanks all — leaving thread open for any new regression reports. Will follow up with a short postmortem once INFRA-1248 has initial PRs.
